summary: Page A8 (jump page, continuations from A1). Target item is a TSC (Trenton State College) jump story on freshman orientation and minority retention rates; it lists 'Utimme Umana/La Voz Oculta' as one of TSC's roughly 20 minority organizations, describing it as 'the minority magazine.' Story cites administrators Alfred Bridges and Sue Baldwin-Way on African-American and Latino freshman retention, scholarships, and mentoring. Other page items: statewide Whitman-vs-Florio poll, state budget/tax coverage, a fall-movie-season feature, a Pemberton Township school bus accident, and a National Archives/McGovern-tapes dispute story.

people.name: Alfred Bridges

people.name: Sue Baldwin-Way

incidents.what: TSC orientation guide lists Utimme Umana/La Voz Oculta among about 20 minority student organizations on campus, describing it as the minority magazine

connections: Utimme Umana/La Voz Oculta appears here as an established campus minority publication at Trenton State College in 1993, seventeen years after the 1976 Trenton State arming-of-campus-police story where it was described as a weekly minority publication opposing the policy -- same outlet, longer institutional life
